tutorial_prompts: Swipe up to ollie over the gap.
Hold the left side to steer into the curve.
Tap twice fast to land a double kick.
Drag back and release to launch.
Pinch to zoom the map out.
Hold jump longer to clear tall rails.
Tap the glowing door to step inside.
Swipe down mid-air to slam the ground.
Tilt left or right to balance on the wire.
Tap the coin icon to open the shop.
Hold block when the red flash appears.
Slide your thumb in a circle to spin.
Tap the camera to snap a photo.
Release at the green mark for a perfect boost.
Tap pause any time to rest your thumbs.
dj_patter: This is Gull Radio 99, loud from the pier to the park.
DJ Rusty Hinge here, keeping your speakers warm.
Traffic report: everyone is late, nobody is sorry.
Next up, a tune my aunt swears cured her hiccups.
Low Tide FM, the station that never checks the clock.
Shout out to the kid skating backward past the bakery.
Weather says drizzle, but the beat says sunshine.
Call in now and tell me your worst wipeout.
That song was older than my van, and my van is ancient.
Night shift crew, this next one is for your coffee.
Mayor Pellet says slow down. We say turn it up.
You are tuned to Dockside 104, home of the bass.
If you hear sirens, that is just the drummer again.
DJ Marla Static spinning till the streetlights quit.
Somebody left a scooter on the bridge. Was that you?
Ten in a row with zero commercials. Mostly.
Keep your knees bent and your volume high.
This track goes out to the pigeons on Fifth Pier.
Static Hour starts now, so grab your headphones.
That is the show, folks. Rusty Hinge signing off.
cutscene_captions: The harbor lights flickered as the last ferry left.
Somewhere across town, a deal was going very wrong.
Three days later, the skatepark was finally open.
The boss never forgot a face, or a debt.
Rain hammered the rooftops while the crew planned.
Nobody had seen the old lighthouse lit in years.
The map was torn, but the X was still there.
By sunrise, every wall in the district had a new tag.
The van coughed, sputtered, and somehow started.
One phone call changed the whole night.
The crowd went silent as the final heat began.
And just like that, the city belonged to them.
